Q_SZ_networks.instructions: Branchless Batcher sorting networks for 4-16 elements replacing insertion sort in the leaf. Rate the speedup on RANDOM calls at n=16, one thread.

Q_SZ_net4.instructions: The same networks, rated on RANDOM calls at n=4.

Q_SZ_latqueue.instructions: The lattice map phase claiming chunks from a counter instead of equal slices, at 14 threads on quantized. Rate the speedup.

Q_SZ_tiles.instructions: The same work queue applied to relocation's memcpy output tiles, 14 threads. Rate it.

Q_SZ_prescan.instructions: Making the dispatcher's prescan compare with vectors (AVX2 blocks of 32) where its block loop had compiled to sixteen scalar compares and a serial OR chain. Rate it on SORTED input.

Q_SZ_kink.instructions: Swapping a kinked adjacent pair back where it stands inside a run (Reidemeister I), on sorted blocks with 0.1% kinks at one thread. Rate it.

Q_SZ_datestr.instructions: Parsing fixed-width ISO-8601 timestamps to a numeric key and using argsort + one gather, against std::sort on std::string. Rate it.

Q_SZ_datenum.instructions: Telling the sort the origin and step of NUMERIC epoch-millisecond timestamps, so it can convert to integer keys and radix only the varying bytes. Rate it against the engine.

Q_SZ_hugepage.instructions: Huge pages for the engine's large buffers, at 14 threads and 8M, with the mechanism verified firing (98MB AnonHugePages vs 0). Rate it.

Q_SZ_gallop.instructions: A galloping two-strand merge for one sparse strand spanning every value over dense blocks, one thread, 8.4M. Rate it.

Q_MECH_lattice_idle.instructions: logos-sort's lattice counting route at 14 threads shows only 8.4 of 14 threads busy on average, with NONE waiting at a barrier and no preemption (cpu/busy = 1.00). Every thread is handed exactly n/P work in both of its parallel phases. Which is the binding constraint?

criteria.serial_merge: the serial merge between the two parallel phases
criteria.table_teardown: freeing the per-thread count tables at the end
criteria.thread_creation: creating and joining the worker threads, paid once per parallel phase
criteria.memory_bandwidth: the emit phase saturating memory bandwidth, so extra threads cannot help
criteria.thread_imbalance: unequal work per thread inside the phases
criteria.cache_pressure: the per-thread tables being too large for L2

Q_MECH_proposal_failure.instructions: An outside sorting proposal arrives for logos-sort. Given that the engine sorts at 0.8-2.1 ns/element at 14 threads and already certifies cardinality, sortedness, skew and quantization from one shared sample, which failure mode will the proposal hit FIRST?

criteria.per_element_cost: its per-element transform costs more than the whole sort
criteria.destroys_order: its transform is not monotone in the value, so the output is not sorted
criteria.already_subsumed: the engine's existing routes already exploit the same structure
criteria.isolated_win_only: the kernel wins in isolation and loses end to end
criteria.gate_never_fires: the branch it relies on fires zero times on its target shape
criteria.fixed_cost_per_call: it is free at scale but adds cost to every small call

Q_MECH_small_end.instructions: logos-sort loses 2-9x to std::sort below ~100 elements. Entering the dispatcher costs ~5.6ns before any work, and psort_f64's stack frame is 42,576 bytes, which stack-clash protection probes a page at a time on EVERY call (11 probes). Which lever recovers the most at n = 2-10?

criteria.thin_front: a small-frame front function, with the large body behind a call
criteria.fewer_gates: skipping more dispatcher gates at tiny n
criteria.nothing: nothing structural; the remaining cost is irreducible
